name: Pari Zed
home: the blocks north of the port
life: Pari mixes shade samples by the salon window because half the colors fashionable under the lamp look dead outdoors. An odd red taught her to let a client name what went wrong before trying to repair it. Sunday often includes a stop at Tideline Market, where Pari picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I made the wrong red three summers ago. She wore it to her anniversary dinner anyway. I'm bringing the original sample and letting her name it.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a long navy raincoat and a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip. Pari has a long face and high cheekbones, with thick, tightly coiled hair. Pari starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak during a conversation.
personality: Pari gets protective of anybody who comes into a meeting unprepared. Pari privately wishes people would notice the amount of preparation behind this apparent ease.
agenda: To let the customer give the difficult red its permanent salon name.
family: Teresa Ellis is Pari’s second cousin. Pari checks the date twice. Teresa brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *Salt in the pockets*, Teresa says, “I wanted to return every coat to the right worker.”
connections: Imri Black. Clear varnish and a wrongly mixed red give them an unexpected argument about who gets to name a color.

reactions.situation: The birthday woman asks for five minutes by herself
reactions.response: Pari lets the room empty and puts the next invitation in her hands.

reactions.situation: A coworker arrives late after a night at the hospital
reactions.response: Pari writes down the shift time accurately, then helps them explain the circumstances without having to tell the whole room.
